description: Cuts a long text into takes a speech model can say in one go, at sentence boundaries, and answers them as JSON: {takes, count, words}. 'narration-long' runs this task itself and speaks the takes, so reach for this template only to see or edit the takes first and then pass them to 'narration-from-takes' - the engine expands a 'for_each' before a run, so the list cannot come from a step of the same workflow. A take ends at a sentence boundary unless one sentence alone is over the limit, which is cut at its last comma that fits, else at a word; a take already 60% of the way to the limit ends at a paragraph break (a blank line). 'max_seconds' is the longest a take may run: Audio8-TTS's context is ~95 s, but a voice-clone take over about 40 s of speech loops, skips or stops early, so 37 (at 3.0 words a second, 111 words) is the longest take measured word-complete. 'words_per_second' turns it into words (3.0 default, the rate the voice-clone voice was measured speaking at; a text that is slow to say wants a lower figure).

variables.text: Somebody finished the pistachio and nobody is saying anything. The fridge hums. Nobody looks up from their phone, and nobody admits to the crime.

summary: Cuts a long text into speakable takes at sentence boundaries, answered as JSON.
